history.summary: The generic 'Sri Rama Temple [Nizamabad]' best maps to the Dichpally Ramalayam (Khilla Ramalayam) - the famous Rama temple of Nizamabad district - NOT Nizamabad town itself. CSV town is approximate: the temple is at Dichpally village in Nizamabad district, on a hillock reached by ~105 steps (Wikipedia; one video description says 108 - minor conflict). Identity certainty: MODERATE-HIGH - this is the best-supported referent, but a second candidate exists: the Qilla Ramalayam (Raghunatha/Ram temple) atop Nizamabad Fort, an ancient Ram shrine on the fort hill in Nizamabad city itself. If the CSV intended the town temple, that is the alternate. The Dichpally temple is built of black and white basalt in Kakatiya style with fine carvings of goddesses, animals and Khajuraho-style erotic sculptures on walls, ceilings, pillars and doorframes - hence the name 'Indhoor Khajuraho' / 'Khajuraho of Nizamabad'. Scholars note four-petal flowers engraved on the stones, a Kakatiya art motif. The complex is enclosed by a masonry wall with bastions at the four corners and a gateway facing north; a pedestrian subway connects to the Raghunanda Temple.

name: Sri Rama Temple
town: Dichpally (CSV town 'Nizamabad' is approximate - the temple is at Dichpally village, Nizamabad district, ~15 km from Nizamabad city; a second candidate is the Qilla Ramalayam atop Nizamabad Fort in Nizamabad town itself)
town_description: Dichpally is a village in Nizamabad district known for the Khilla Ramalayam on its hillock. The temple precinct sits atop the hill reached by a flight of steps, with a masonry enclosure wall; it is the 'Indhoor Khajuraho' of the district and a noted day-trip destination from Nizamabad city.
